correctness.rationale: Diagonalization by all product-group characters gives degree-\(k\) eigenvalues with multiplicity \(\binom nk(r-1)^k\). For \(0<q\le u_n\), each shifted alternating sum is positive except the top-degree sum F_n. Exact inequalities prove \(F_n(1/n)>0\), \(F_n(u_n)<0\) and \(F_n\) strictly decreasing on \([0,u_n]\). Thus one first root yields positive definiteness below, nullity \((r-1)^n\) at equality, and a negative eigenvalue immediately above; the generality in \(r\) is exact. Binomial-series error \(O(n^{-6})\), derivative order n and formal expansion give the stated \(O(n^{-7})\) root correction. Exact finite checker run from included code passed 2074 assertions/character comparisons.

value.rationale: The first bandwidth at which the squared-Hamming Gaussian fails to be a valid covariance or completely positive Schur multiplier is a natural exact invariant. Universal alphabet independence is not visible from the general spectrum, as all lower Fourier modes have alphabet-dependent coefficients. The exact high-multiplicity nullspace and logarithmic critical bandwidth with explicit correction are useful quantitative boundaries; an all-mode comparison is essential, not a routine reparameterization.
